title: Guarujá triplex and storage of the presidential collection
status: Triplex case closed as time-barred in 2022
summary: Federal prosecutors accused Lula of receiving benefits from OAS through a triplex apartment and renovations. The convictions were annulled in 2021, and the case was closed as time-barred in January 2022.
details: The STJ had imposed a sentence of eight years, ten months and twenty days in 2019, later annulled. The closure ruling also preserved the earlier acquittal on the presidential collection storage charge, which prosecutors could no longer appeal. In June 2026, a dispute over proceeds from the apartment auction was reported to have been sent back to the Federal District courts.
defense: Lula denied owning the triplex or receiving bribes. Welcoming the closure, his lawyers said the case had been used for political persecution.
limit: Annulment and the statute of limitations are not an acquittal on the merits of the triplex charges. The acquittal concerning the collection is separate. The property dispute reported in 2026 does not establish that the criminal case reopened.

title: Renovations at the Atibaia country property
status: Punishability extinguished; prosecution appeal denied in 2025
summary: Lula faced corruption and money laundering charges over renovations funded by contractors at a country property he visited. After the convictions were annulled, a Federal District court held the charges time-barred in 2021; the TRF1 upheld closure in 2025.
details: The 2019 conviction, upheld by the TRF4 in 2020, was invalidated in 2021. The Federal District court rejected the ratified complaint and extinguished Lula’s punishability. Rejection also covered charges already resulting in acquittals or duplicated in another case. In July 2025, the TRF1’s Tenth Panel denied the prosecution appeal; the judgment’s report was reproduced in the August national judicial gazette.
defense: The defense denied the allegations and said the 2021 ruling reinforced its claim of judicial persecution. No specific response to the appeal decided in 2025 was located.
limit: The annulled conviction is no longer valid. The statute of limitations, rejection of charges and preservation of earlier acquittals are distinct grounds. The certificate confirming finality of the 2025 judgment was not directly verified.

title: Land for Instituto Lula and the neighboring apartment
court: Federal courts in Paraná and the Federal District · STF
status: Criminal proceedings terminated in 2023
summary: Lula became a defendant in 2016 on allegations that Odebrecht provided benefits through land intended for his institute and an apartment next to his home. The STF terminated the case in 2023.
details: Both properties formed part of the same corruption and money laundering prosecution. Instituto Lula never occupied the land. After Curitiba’s acts were annulled in 2021, the proceedings were suspended. On 17 February 2023, Ricardo Lewandowski terminated prosecution for lack of sufficient grounds after evidence from Odebrecht’s leniency agreement was invalidated.
defense: The defense denied that Lula had received ownership or possession of the properties as a benefit for Petrobras contracts. It also challenged the evidence’s validity and sought termination.
limit: Termination for lack of sufficient grounds is distinct from acquittal following a trial on the merits. Land and apartment are grouped because they were in the same case; this record does not attribute to Lula all amounts investigated in relation to others.

title: Odebrecht donations to Instituto Lula
court: Federal courts in Paraná and the Federal District · STF
status: Criminal proceedings terminated in 2023
summary: Lula was prosecuted for allegedly laundering R$4 million transferred by Odebrecht to the institute in 2013 and 2014. The STF terminated the case in February 2023.
details: The complaint accepted in October 2020 alleged that four donations concealed unlawful benefits. The case was transferred from Curitiba and suspended in 2021. Closure in 2023 followed the absence of valid evidentiary support after material derived from the contractor’s leniency agreement was invalidated.
defense: Cristiano Zanin said the donations were lawful, supported by receipts and recorded in the accounts. The defense sought closure after the evidence was excluded.
limit: Proceedings were actually instituted against Lula even though the entity received the transfers. Termination is neither a conviction nor an acquittal following a trial on the merits. This case is separate from ARG company donations associated with Equatorial Guinea.

title: Zelotes — automotive incentives under Provisional Measure 471
status: Acquitted for insufficient evidence
summary: Lula faced a bribery charge concerning Provisional Measure 471/2009. He was acquitted on 21 June 2021 after prosecutors themselves found insufficient evidence for conviction.
details: The charge linked extended incentives for automakers to an alleged R$6 million payment to the PT. The judgment found insufficient proof of Lula’s involvement and applied Article 386(VII) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
defense: The defense also sought invalidation of the charges over evidence deemed unlawful by the Supreme Court; the acquittal made that request moot.
limit: This prosecution is separate from Gripen/Provisional Measure 627. The judgment orders closure once final; it does not itself certify finality.

court: Supreme Federal Court · 10th Federal Criminal Court, Federal District
status: Prosecution terminated by the Supreme Court in 2023
summary: Lula was charged with influence peddling, money laundering and criminal organization in proceedings concerning Gripen fighters and Provisional Measure 627/2013. The Supreme Court terminated the prosecution in February 2023.
details: Ricardo Lewandowski suspended the prosecution in 2022 and granted habeas corpus on his own initiative on 17 February 2023. He identified a lack of sufficient grounds and compromised evidence linked to coordination with the Curitiba task force.

limit: Termination over procedural defects and insufficient grounds is distinct from acquittal after a trial on the merits. Provisional Measure 471 concerns a separate prosecution.

title: Obstruction of justice — Nestor Cerveró’s testimony
court: 10th Federal Court, Federal District · Federal Regional Court of the 1st Region
status: Acquittal upheld on appeal
summary: Lula faced charges of participating in an attempt to prevent Nestor Cerveró from cooperating with investigators. He was acquitted in 2018; the appellate court upheld the decision in 2019.
details: The judgment discussed flaws in the evidence and cooperating witnesses’ accounts. Its operative order acquitted under Article 386(III): the act does not constitute a criminal offense.
defense: The defense sought acquittal and challenged the charges and cooperation evidence. Prosecutors had also requested Lula’s acquittal at trial.
limit: The judgment’s express legal basis should not be replaced by the generic label of insufficient evidence. No certificate of finality was reviewed.

title: ARG — donation and business in Equatorial Guinea

limit: Termination is not an acquittal on the merits. The ruling limits its relief to Lula; the codefendant’s outcome is not inferred.
